extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners (PRSA members and communicators advising organizations/clients)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and enforceable-adjacent standards from PRSA's Board of Ethics and Professional Standards (BEPS) for ethical practice in public relations, covering topics such as disclosure, social media, AI accountability, plagiarism, paid placements, leaks, and related conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Code of Ethics (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRSA Code of Ethics is widely regarded as the cornerstone of the ethical practice of public relations. It applies to PRSA members and is designed to be a useful guide as they carry out their ethical responsibilities, setting out principles that uphold core values, including advocacy, honesty, expertise, independence, loyalty and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA can establish voluntary practice standards, inspire and educate best practice, promote voluntary compliance, and set reasonable procedures for membership. The Code exists to inspire ethical behavior, identify improper practices, and teach members how to avoid them. PRSA's enforcement authority is limited; BEPS provides educational resources, case studies, position papers and ESAs to interpret and apply the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-Play
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay-for-play: when payment is required for development and publishing of content (blog posts, videos, interviews, columns, etc.), creating a transaction in which payor makes undisclosed payments to a media channel to feature specific content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS's position: pay-for-play conflicts with the Code and deceives consumers by hiding that content was paid for rather than selected on merit. It violates at least Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. How to avoid: request and include disclosure with the final information product where compensation was provided; encourage journalists/bloggers/digital operators to disclose travel, lodging, gifts or non-monetary compensation; always encourage clear and obvious disclosure of material value or compensation. Note: FTC guidelines may require labeling in some commercial contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics & Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Because social platforms are largely unmonitored and unregulated through an ethics prism and reach billions, PR practitioners must incorporate a higher standard of practice and apply the PRSA Code in all social media strategies and tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key Code provisions for social media include Disclosure of Information, Safeguarding Confidences, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Guidance includes: content providers should fully disclose paid placements and associations; protect confidential and private information (risk of improper disclosure via social channels); be aware of employee free-speech rights (NLRB); disclose conflicts of interest when communicating; require proper FTC-style disclosures for influencers/product samples; ensure gifts are nominal, legal and infrequent; use social media to inform and educate while sharing best practices. Trust is the ultimate currency — build credibility through transparency and ethical behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is the unauthorized use or close imitation of another creator's language and thoughts and presenting that content as your own original work; it can be intentional or inadvertent and is ethically equivalent in PRSA's view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: inadvertent plagiarism carries equal weight with intentional misrepresentation. Practitioners must attribute and, as appropriate, pay licensing compensation. How to avoid: do not copy sentences/paragraphs/documents even if edited; use your own words and paraphrase; give proper credit when paraphrasing; use quotation marks and credit the source when copying exact wording; disclose all sources; when using internet sources, recognize creators are entitled to credit. Plagiarism may overlap with copyright issues but remains an ethical standard regardless of copyright status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid Spokespersons and Influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone paid to serve as a spokesperson, advocate or influencer for an organization, company, brand or special interest must disclose the contractual arrangement or the relationship with the sponsor providing compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice implicates Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. BEPS recommends: commercial relationships be disclosed in advance of or simultaneous to the same public forum so affected publics can make informed decisions; every party in the contractual relationship has an obligation to disclose; failure to disclose is improper conduct under the Code; be honest and accurate in all communications; reveal sponsors and any financial interests that may affect outcomes. Treat influencer arrangements consistently with FTC guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing Front Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A front group is an organization created or labeled to mislead the public about its true mission; creating or assisting such groups deceives the public by hiding true intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: any effort to deceive the public or others is a clear violation of the PRSA Code of Ethics. Relevant Code provisions include Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendation: PRSA members should avoid assisting front groups or individuals representing undisclosed sponsorships or deceptive descriptions of goals, sponsors, or tactics, even if activities are lawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Fees or Compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Overstating charges, fees or compensation (claiming compensation/credit for work never performed) is unethical and harms the profession and clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS's position: members who provide PR services should charge clients only for services rendered and in accordance with contracts. Guidance: properly report services rendered, time spent, out-of-pocket charges and related fees; avoid inflating or overstating charges or supporting data. Primary Code linkage: Enhancing the Profession; professional values implicated include honesty, fairness and loyalty. Members should pledge to adhere to rigid conduct and integrity standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Advertising & Sponsored Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Native advertising and sponsored content mimic organic content and can blur the lines between paid and unpaid content, often making it difficult for consumers to distinguish sponsorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: distinguish clearly between organic and sponsored content and clearly identify the sponsor. Relevant Code provisions include Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Competition, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: disclosures should be clear and appropriate to the medium; sponsored content should be easily discernable from organic content; disclosures should effectively differentiate paid content and must not attempt to deceive consumers into believing content is independent or objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Leadership Accountabilities (Machine Learning Accountabilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: As AI and machine learning make decisions formerly made by humans, accountability for mistakes should rest with human beings with active oversight at the time of the decision, not with the machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: organizations and leadership with oversight responsibility will be held accountable and should take responsibility for identifying root causes and corrective actions with transparency. Relevant Code provisions include Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: counsel senior leadership that machines cannot be held accountable; clearly draw and present lines of human responsibility when developing communications and responses involving AI; ensure transparency about who is responsible for oversight and corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media as a Reflection of Majority Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media activity is not a scientifically vetted indicator of majority public opinion; a small percentage of active users often drives much of the visible activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: communicators should not presume social media equals majority opinion. When sharing analysis based on social media, remind audiences that the platform is an informal, non-scientific source and may not reflect general public sentiment. Relevant Code provisions include Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, and Enhancing the Profession. Practitioners should present social-media-derived analysis with appropriate caveats and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications professionals often have access to confidential or proprietary information; leaking such information without authorization undermines trust and can be illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: members should refrain from leaking information to media or stakeholders without expressed approval of organizational leadership. Relevant Code provisions include Safeguarding Confidences, Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: be aware of laws, regulations, contracts and business terms governing information flow; adhere to contractual and legal obligations; never autonomously share information obtained in confidence; follow procedures for approving disclosure; understand potential criminal/civil penalties for illegal leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS issues Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs) to provide guidance within the framework of the Code when new issues arise; ESAs are informational and not legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESAs interpret Code provisions and provide recommendations (e.g., ESA on misinformation, Pay-for-Play advisories). A complete list of ESAs is available to members on MyPRSA. ESAs are designed to educate and guide members in evolving ethical situations and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect and advance the free flow of accurate and truthful information which is essential to serving the public interest and contributing to informed decision-making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoked across topics (pay-for-play, native advertising, plagiarism, front groups, social media). Practitioners should prioritize accuracy and truth, avoid deception, and ensure information promotes informed public decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build trust with the public through all communications by revealing all information needed for responsible decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires disclosure of paid placements, commercial relationships, sponsorships, conflicts of interest, gifts of material value, and other material facts. Disclosures should be clear, appropriate to medium, and timely (in advance of or simultaneous to communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest to build the trust of clients, employers and the publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act in clients' best interest, avoid circumstances that compromise judgement, disclose existing or potential conflicts promptly, and require practitioners to be transparent about relationships that may affect objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work to strengthen the public's trust in the profession, acknowledging an obligation to protect and enhance the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uphold standards that build respect and credibility for PR; avoid practices that damage the profession's reputation (e.g., undisclosed pay-for-play, plagiarism, overstating fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the privacy rights of clients, organizations and individuals by safeguarding confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special care required when using or sharing information via social media or other public channels; respect NDAs and legal/regulatory constraints; do not share confidential information without authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote healthy and fair competition among professionals while preserving intellectual property rights in the marketplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid practices that infringe on IP or unfairly claim another's work; respect competitors while fostering a robust business environment; protect market integrity in sponsored/native content contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Value — Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should ensure communications are accurate, avoid deception, appropriately attribute sources, and correct errors promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Value — Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treating others with respect, avoiding deceptive practices, disclosing pertinent information and ensuring equitable treatment in commercial and editorial interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Value — Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide objective counsel to those we represent; be accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain objectivity, avoid undue influence by sponsors or commercial interests, disclose relationships that could compromise independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Value — Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent; support marketplace of ideas and informed public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy must be balanced with transparency and honesty; when authors or sponsors are fully disclosed, advocacy aids informed debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Value — Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience; advance the profession through continued development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use skill and judgment responsibly, continually update knowledge (e.g., on AI, social media, legal/regulatory changes) and apply that expertise ethically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Value — Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Be faithful to those we represent while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance client loyalty with public interest obligations; do not act in ways that deceive the public or undermine trust in the profession.
